summary: Reproduced the defect live: generate-todo.sh takes 6.9s against the real 636KB/101-task state.json, exceeding both the 5000ms scope-mutex acquire budget and the 10s staleness window. Root cause is jq subprocess-spawn count (~1000+ spawns), not file size. Also found the acquire budget is a hardcoded, non-overridable constant in task-lock.sh, so passing a larger stale_sec alone cannot fix the spurious-ABORT failure mode. Recommend combining WORK items 1 (move generate-todo.sh out of state-write.sh's owned-here critical section, preserving guest-mode behavior unchanged) + 3 (single-pass jq rewrite of generate-todo.sh) + 4 (regression test); item 2 is optional defense-in-depth only.
decisions_made: Fix combines WORK items 1+3+4; item 2 (stale_sec>=30) is optional hardening, not required, since SCOPE_MUTEX_ACQUIRE_BUDGET_MS=5000 in task-lock.sh is hardcoded with no override path and item 1 alone drops the critical section to a measured 13ms

state-write.sh change must release the mutex early only in owned-here mode (call release_mutex before generate-todo.sh); guest mode (nested under orchestrator-postflight.sh's own 30s-staleness bracket) must be left unchanged since release_mutex is already a no-op there
No task-lock.sh changes are required to meet the verification bar; it stays in file_scope only for an optional item-2 hardening

generate-todo.sh's single-pass jq rewrite (item 3) should be its own reviewable phase separate from the state-write.sh mutex-release change (item 1), gated by a TODO.md content-identity check against the pre-rewrite fixture
